facts.statement: Harrington Health provided a sample extract containing real patient names, dates of birth, and diagnosis codes on September 12, 2026.
facts.quote: It's real data I think — names, DOBs, some diagnosis codes.
facts.whyItMatters: Regulated patient data (PHI) was received before the Business Associate Agreement (BAA) has been signed.

facts.statement: The Harrington Health patient data was forwarded to team members in Pune, India for profiling.
facts.quote: Pranav opened it here and forwarded to Sneha and Vikram in Pune to start profiling.
facts.whyItMatters: PHI was transferred to an offshore location while the BAA (still in review) reportedly restricts data access to the US.

facts.statement: Daniel Ortiz, a US-based freelance data engineer, is being staffed to handle patient data to satisfy US-only requirements in the BAA.
facts.quote: the BAA says nobody outside the US touches patient data, so he's bringing in Daniel Ortiz, freelance data engineer in Austin.
facts.whyItMatters: Contractor status and BAA coverage for Daniel Ortiz must be verified to ensure compliance with the client's US-only data requirements.

facts.statement: The Harrington Health MSA and BAA are required to be signed by October 1, 2026.
facts.quote: Harrington (Dhaval) — $210k, US, their paper — by 1 Oct
facts.whyItMatters: This is a critical deadline for closing the $210k deal on the counterparty's paper.

facts.statement: The Harrington BAA requires $5M in cyber insurance coverage, exceeding the company's current $1M policy.
facts.quote: Our cyber policy is $1M btw, Harrington BAA wants 5.
facts.whyItMatters: The agreement creates a financial commitment for higher insurance coverage that is not currently met.
